## DupFinder 1.2.0: safer web page, pinned FFmpeg, English everywhere

Finding duplicates works as in 1.1.0. What you notice: the page and the console are in English now, and the address of the page carries a one-time key.

- **Only your own browser tab gets in:** the page now answers only the tab DupFinder opened (a one-time key, new on every start, and a check of the host name). Before, a malicious web page open at the same time could, with some effort, reach DupFinder and move files to the recycle bin. If you close the tab, open the link shown in the DupFinder window again.
- **Delete moves only files of the group:** DupFinder refuses any file that is not part of the group you confirm.
- **One fixed FFmpeg build:** on first run DupFinder downloads exactly one FFmpeg build (9.0.2), checked by size and SHA-256 before anything is unpacked, from its own mirror or from the original source. Before, it took the newest daily build, unchecked. An FFmpeg already in your `bin` folder stays in use.
- **Your decisions are safe:** if `ignored.json` or `session.json` cannot be read (e.g. after a power failure), DupFinder keeps it next to it as `.broken-<date>` and tells you, instead of starting over and overwriting it. All files are written so that a crash never leaves half a file.
- **No duplicates found:** the page now says so instead of staying empty.
- **Clearer messages:** problems at start say what happened and what to do; a double-click on `DupFinder.exe` without a folder keeps the window open so you can read how to use it. `DupFinder.exe -version` prints the version.
- **Tidier:** FFmpeg processes end together with DupFinder, even if it crashes; the log file stays below 2 MB plus three older parts.
- **English:** page, console and messages are in English, like the README and the website.

Update: replace `DupFinder.exe` with the new one. Your decisions, the ignore list and the FFmpeg in `bin` next to it stay. The release now also carries `SHA256SUMS.txt` to check the download.
